request.prompt: View 1, the approach from the south, at dusk in steady rain. The eye stands on the flat valley floor beside a small roofless wayside shrine with a lit fire, looking north. A straight pilgrim road runs away from the viewer and climbs a stone stair onto a long narrow stone bridge, the Hanging Causeway, raised about twelve blocks above the valley floor on square piers. The causeway ends at a squat fortified barbican gatehouse with a shut portcullis. Behind it a steep rock crag carries the castle: a square outer curtain wall enclosing a large courtyard, a long straight east rampart wall walk running north on the right, a tall rectangular keep with long pointed Gothic windows in the centre back, a cloister and a tall chapel with a rose window on the left, and far back on the left a slender square bell tower with an open belfry at its top, its great bell visibly cracked. Parts of the roofs have fallen in. Grey mist pools at the foot of the crag. The mountain rim of the bowl closes the horizon on every side.
request.style_note: Vesperhold, a half-ruined Gothic castle standing on a rock crag in the middle of a wide mountain bowl, drawn in the same hand throughout: dark-fantasy concept painting, muted slate-grey, ash and moss-green palette with small warm accents of candle and fire light, soft rain haze, confident painterly brushwork with crisp readable architectural silhouettes, massing built from large squared stone blocks with flat faces and clean right angles so every form could be built block by block. Each image is ONE single full-frame view of that place, filling the frame edge to edge: never a sheet, never a grid, never a panel, never an inset, never a caption, label, text or border.
